about: The mutant ledger of internal/gocmd, the toolchain front of `ergo go` (ERGO-GO). Run it with go run ./scripts/mutants internal/gocmd; the killers that build Go are cmd/ergo's full-tier acceptance tests.

mutants.name: gocmd-gcflags-accumulate
mutants.rule: cmd/go gives a package the flags of the last -gcflags value that matches it, whole (PerPackageFlag.For), so ergo's -ergoir value carries exactly the user's flags for the package.

mutants.name: gocmd-gcflags-unnamed
mutants.to: match := func(Package) bool { return named && false }
mutants.rule: A -gcflags value without a pattern applies to the packages named on the command line.

mutants.name: gocmd-relative-by-path
mutants.from: return func(p Package) bool { return p.Dir == dir }
mutants.to: return func(p Package) bool { return p.ImportPath == dir }
mutants.rule: A relative package pattern matches a package by its folder, as cmd/go's MatchPackage does.

mutants.name: gocmd-mixed-allowed
mutants.rule: One package is one language (owner q296): a folder of .ergo files with a Go file of its own package is refused.

mutants.name: gocmd-xtest-refused
mutants.rule: A Go test of package NAME_test beside the .ergo files is Go importing the Ergo package, and is allowed.

mutants.name: gocmd-testdata-walked
mutants.rule: The module's Ergo packages are its folders as ./... walks them: testdata is skipped.

mutants.name: gocmd-no-ergoir
mutants.rule: Each Ergo package's compile is given its IR (-gcflags=PKG=-ergoir=FILE): its declarations have no Go bodies.

mutants.name: gocmd-no-overlay
mutants.rule: The declaration file reaches the Ergo package's folder through -overlay, so Go imports it by its import path.

mutants.name: gocmd-no-runtime
mutants.rule: The go.mod copy requires Ergo's runtime module and replaces it with ergo's cached copy.

mutants.name: gocmd-asset-by-folder
mutants.rule: An asset is overlaid into the folder of the Go package that embeds it (assets/DIGEST/… below it), and its package's tree holds it.
